A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D8-equivariant ViT research, despite the change from Octic Vision Transformers to Quick ViTs. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original supervised and self-supervised experiments, segmentation and hematology evaluations, architectural ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V5 retains original experimental results and adds linear-layer benchmarks, training-throughput measurements, and 45-degree rotation results.

M1.justification: The D8-equivariant patch embedding, Fourier-domain linear layers, nonlinearities, normalization, attention, invariantization, and hybrid architectures remain unchanged. Quick ViTs is a renaming; the larger-dihedral-group discussion extends theoretical analysis without establishing an implemented method change.

E1.justification: The classification, segmentation, and hematology datasets are retained. V5 Appendix F.4 and Table 12 add a 45-degree rotation scenario beyond the existing 90-degree tests, extending input-condition coverage without adding a new application domain.

E2.justification: The DeiT comparison drops D2 and D8 models at both sizes, while the DINOv2 comparison drops D8(ViT-L/16). Standard ViT and H2 comparisons remain. V5 Table 2 introduces an eight-equal-block diagonal linear-layer comparator alongside standard and D8 layers.

E3.justification: V5 adds controlled linear-layer benchmarking across fp16/fp32 and widths 1024/8192, using F=4C and 64×196 tokens on an A100-80GB. It also adds forward-plus-backward training timing and 45-degree rotation testing. These substantially extend evaluation design; the retained DeiT/DINOv2 training recipes and hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test how precision and width explain the FLOP-to-throughput gap, whether inference savings extend to training, and whether robustness extends outside exact D8 rotations. The existing invariantization, equivariance-breaking, layer-count, and learned-filter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain averaging over 1000 forward passes for nonlinearity benchmarks and 100 runs after 10 warm-ups for general throughput. Neither adds training-seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained headline accuracy values are unchanged, but substantial new efficiency and robustness results appear. V5 reports D8 linear-layer speedups of 2.6× in fp16 versus 4.8× in fp32 at 1024→4096 channels, training-throughput results, and 45-degree accuracy drops. It also removes main-table results such as D8(ViT-L/16)'s 72.2% DINOv2 linear ImageNet accuracy.

T1.justification: V5 Appendix C extends the D8 analysis to D4n, deriving block structure, a 4n²/(2n−1) FLOP-saving factor, and generalized arithmetic intensity. Section 4.1 also adds large-batch limiting arguments and arithmetic intensity for the eight-block comparator. The original D8 mathematics remains.

C1.justification: The central architecture, approximately 40% FLOP-saving claim, and preserved-accuracy claims remain. V5 adds an explicit abstract/introduction contribution identifying hardware- and precision-dependent limits on converting FLOP savings into throughput.

C2.justification: V5 expands the existing arithmetic-intensity discussion into a more explicit explanation of throughput bottlenecks. It also explains H8's advantage through useful upright-orientation information in ImageNet and adds applicability discussion concerning 3D vision and feature matching.

D1.justification: V3's complete per-experiment GPU-hour accounting, aggregate compute budget, and licensing/data-access section are removed. Conversely, v5 changes code-release wording from planned to available and documents additional benchmark settings and existing throughput precision more explicitly. Core implementation details and training hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: V5 adds discussion and citations concerning learned approximate equivariance, DINOv3, and newer feature-matching and 3D work. The hierarchical/SparseViT comparison is replaced by discussion of complementarity with pruning and quantization. Positioning relative to the retained reflection-equivariant predecessor emphasizes broader evaluation and arithmetic-intensity analysis.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change to Quick ViTs, and the abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Method motivation is expanded, computational efficiency becomes a standalone section, and the appendices are reorganized. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: V5 adopts a different document template with narrower text blocks, running headers, and separate supplementary pagination. It adds three experimental tables, removes the GPU-hour table, shortens the main comparison tables, and revises captions and ratio displays. The underlying content of Figures 1–7 is largely retained.

improvement.justification: Precision-controlled benchmarks and training timings better support the efficiency claims, while the 45-degree test establishes robustness beyond guaranteed symmetries. These gains outweigh, but are limited by, removal of comparison results and GPU-hour/licensing disclosures. With the implemented method and headline accuracy evidence unchanged, the net quality improvement is limited.
